case.title: Case
case.alternatesIntro: Variants that solve the same case — pick whichever fingertricks work for you.
case.highlightHint: Greyed-out stickers are not part of this stage — they're just there for orientation. Colourful stickers are the area you're working on.

compare.title: Compare two cases
compare.intro: Pick two cases to see their states and algorithms side-by-side.

movement.labelsHint: Numbers mark each piece: n = current position, n′ = where it ends up. Pieces follow the cycle n → n′.

settings.title: Settings
settings.visualAidLabel: Highlight the stickers that move and visualise each turn
settings.visualAidDesc: Greys out stickers that are already in place, shows a face + arrow icon for every move, and reveals a notation legend on each case. Turn off for a denser, expert view.

legend.title: How to read the notation
legend.intro: Each letter names a face of the cube; the symbol after it tells you how to turn it.
legend.suffixes: No suffix = quarter turn clockwise (when looking at that face). An apostrophe (’) means counter-clockwise. A 2 means a half-turn. Lower-case letters are wide turns (face + adjacent slice). M/E/S are middle-slice turns; x/y/z rotate the whole cube.

crossIntro.title: The Cross
crossIntro.body: The cross is the first step of CFOP: build a plus-shape of one colour on the bottom layer with its edge pieces matched to neighbouring centres. Aim for ≤ 8 moves and to look ahead to your first F2L pair while you solve it.

crossPlanning.title: Planning the Cross
crossPlanning.body: Use your 15-second inspection: locate all four cross edges, plan moves that don't disturb edges you've already solved, and watch where the first F2L corner+edge pair will end up so you can attack it without pause.

f2lShapes.title: Three shapes of F2L
f2lShapes.body: Every F2L pair sits in one of three families: pair joined in the top, pair split in the top, or pair stuck in the slot. Recognise which family you have first; the right move follows.

f2lJoined.title: Pair joined in the top
f2lJoined.body: Place the joined pair above its empty slot, then insert with U R U' R' (or the mirrored U' L' U L). Practise from every angle.

f2lSplit.title: Pair split in the top
f2lSplit.body: Bring the corner and edge together using U-moves, then insert. The split case is twelve cases; intuitively you 'unstuck' them by aligning corner-above-slot first.

f2lStuck.title: Stuck in the slot
f2lStuck.body: If the corner or edge is already in the slot but wrong, extract it (R U' R' or similar) to put it back in the top layer, then re-solve as a joined or split case.

eoDot.desc: No edges yet oriented on top.

eoLine.desc: A horizontal line of oriented edges across the top.

eoL.desc: Two adjacent oriented edges forming an L.

aPerm.desc: Three corners cycle; edges already solved.

f2lJoined.desc: Corner and edge are joined in the top layer, sitting next to each other and ready to be inserted into their empty slot.

f2lSplit.desc: Corner and edge are both in the top layer, but separated — first bring them together with a U-move, then insert.

f2lStuck.desc: A pair piece is already wedged into the slot, but in the wrong place. Pop it out first, then re-insert as a joined or split case.

eoDot.notes: Two-shot: first fix one edge, then the rest.
